page: Microsoft Azure F4als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 4 dedicated physical cores running at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, providing 4 vCPUs. Memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB per core. The processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware instruction support for AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), SHA-NI, and VAES.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core execution reaching 3,081.08 points and Geekbench single-core scoring 2,087.0, both placing in the top quartile. Multi-core performance aligns within the middle tier, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 10,620.08 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,710.0. In contrast, memory bandwidth under large uncached read transfers drops to 36.2 GB/sec, placing it in the lower quartile, mirrored by a bottom-tier PassMark memory score of 1,789.97. Text processing and static web serving yield stable median throughput, while LLM inference slows significantly when scaling from small 135M models to 7B models.

The instance does not bundle local disk storage, requiring external premium network-attached disks, and it includes no dedicated GPUs. Cost efficiency is driven primarily by core compute performance rather than memory capacity, making it a targeted fit for compute-bound tasks with small memory footprints, including CI/CD software compilation, batch processing, front-end web serving, and microservices.
description: Microsoft Azure F4als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine equipped with an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz across 4 dedicated x86_64 cores. Configured with a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio, the server supplies 8.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core) and excludes bundled local storage as well as hardware GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core CPU execution, achieving top-tier results in single-threaded stress-ng and Geekbench tests, supported by AVX-512 instruction extensions. Multi-threaded CPU throughput, web serving, and in-memory key-value operations remain squarely in the middle tier, though memory-intensive workloads show lower uncached read bandwidth. Lacking local NVMe disks and extensive RAM, the server delivers balanced cost efficiency for processing-heavy workloads that operate within lean memory boundaries, including code compilation, containerized application serving, batch scripting, and modular microservices.
